source_text:
Καὶ ἡμεῖς οὖν ἐντύχωμεν περὶ τῶν ἔν τινι παραπτώματι ὑπαρχόντων, ὅπως δοθῇ αὐτοῖς ἐπιείκεια καὶ ταπεινοφροσύνη εἰς τὸ εἶξαι αὐτοὺς μὴ ἡμῖν ἀλλὰ τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ: οὕτως γὰρ ἔσται αὐτοῖς ἔγκαρπος καὶ τελεία ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους μετ’ οἰκτιρμῶν μνεία.
ἀναλάβωμεν παιδείαν, ἐφ̓ ᾗ οὐδεὶς ὀφείλει ἀγανακτεῖν, ἀγαπητοί. ἡ νουθέτησις, ἣν ποιούμεθα εἰς ἀλλήλους, καλή ἐστιν καὶ ὑπεράγαν ὠφέλιμος: κολλᾷ γὰρ ἡμᾶς τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ.
οὕτως γάρ φησιν ὁ ἅγιος λόγος: Παιδεύων ἐπαίδευσέν με ὁ κύριος, καὶ τῷ θανάτῳ οὐ παρέδωκέν με:
ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.
Παιδεύσει με γάρ, φησίν, δίκαιος ἐν ἐλέει καὶ ἐλέγξει με, ἔλαιον δὲ ἁμαρτωλῶν μὴ λιπανάτω τὴν κεφαλήν μου.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Μακάριος ἄνθρωπος, ὃν ἤλεγξεν ὁ κύριος: νουθέτημα δὲ παντοκράτορος μὴ ἀπαναίνου: αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀλγεῖν ποιεῖ, καὶ πάλιν ἀποκαθίστησιν:
ἔπαισεν, καὶ αἱ χεῖρες αὐτοῦ ἰάσαντο.
ἑξάκις ἐξ ἀναγκῶν ἐξελεῖταί σε, ἐν δὲ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ οὐχ ἅψεταί σου κακόν.
ἐν λιμῷ ῥύσεταί σε ἐκ θανάτου, ἐν πολέμῳ δὲ ἐκ χειρὸς σιδήρου λύσει σε:
καὶ ἀπὸ μάστιγος γλώσσης σε κρύψει, καὶ οὐ μὴ φοβηθήσῃ κακῶν ἐπερχομένων.
ἀδίκων καὶ ἀνόμων καταγελάσῃ, ἀπὸ δὲ θηρίων ἀγρίων οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇς:
θῆρες γὰρ ἄγριοι εἰρηνεύσουσίν σοι.
εἶτα γνώσῃ, ὅτι εἰρηνεύσει σου ὁ οἶκος, ἡ δὲ δίαιτα τῆς σκηνῆς σου οὐ μὴ ἁμάρτῃ.
γνώσῃ δέ, ὅτι πολὺ τὸ σπέρμα σου, τὰ δὲ τέκνα σου ὥσπερ τὸ παμβότανον τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
ἐλεύσῃ δὲ ἐν τάφῳ ὥσπερ σῖτος ὥριμος κατὰ καιρὸν θεριζόμενος, ἢ ὥσπερ θημωνιὰ ἅλωνος καθ̓ ὤραν συγκομισθεῖσα.
βλέπετε, ἀγαπητοί, πόσος ὑπερασπισμός ἐστιν τοῖς παιδευομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ δεσπότου: πατὴρ γὰρ ἀγαθὸς ὢν παιδεύει εἰς τὸ ἐλεηθῆναι ἡμᾶς διὰ τῆς ὁσίας παιδείας αὐτοῦ.
orientation: The author, writing from the church in Rome, urges the Corinthians to intercede for those caught in wrongdoing and to accept God's corrective discipline as a sign of his fatherly love.
pass_a_gloss: And we therefore let us intercede concerning the [ones] being in any transgression, so that may be given to them gentleness and humility for the [purpose] to yield them not to us but to the will of God; for thus will be to them fruitful and perfect the toward God and the saints with mercies remembrance. Let us take up discipline, at which no one owes to be angry, beloved. The admonition, which we make toward one another, good is and exceedingly beneficial; for it joins us to the will of God. For thus says the holy word: Disciplining he disciplined me the Lord, and to death not he handed over me: for whom he loves [the] Lord disciplines, and he whips every son whom he receives. He will discipline me for, it says, [the] righteous in mercy and he will convict me, but oil of sinners let it not anoint the head of me. And again it says: Blessed [the] man, whom he convicted the Lord; and [the] admonition of [the] Almighty do not reject; for he himself to suffer makes, and again he restores: he struck, and the hands of him healed. Six times from distresses he will deliver you, and in the seventh not will touch you evil. In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war from hand of iron he will release you: and from whip of tongue he will hide you, and not not you will fear evils coming upon [you]. At [the] unjust and lawless you will laugh, and from wild beasts not not you will fear: for wild beasts will be at peace with you. Then you will know, that will be at peace your house, and the dwelling of the tent of you not not will sin. You will know and, that great [is] the seed of you, and the children of you like the all-grass of the field. You will come and in [the] tomb like wheat ripe in season being harvested, or like [a] heap of [a] threshing floor in season gathered in. See, beloved, how great [a] protection is to the [ones] being disciplined by the Master: for [a] father good being he disciplines for the [purpose] to be shown mercy [to] us through the holy discipline of him.

choices.why: The section's central theme is God's corrective discipline; 'discipline' captures both instruction and correction without narrowing to punishment.
The verb means to approach or petition on behalf of others; 'intercede' preserves the prayerful, mediatorial force.
The noun refers to a memorial or mention before God; 'remembrance' keeps the liturgical sense of being remembered before God and the saints.
The noun denotes a shield or defense; 'protection' conveys the safeguarding force of God's discipline.
The rare compound means 'all-herb' or every kind of vegetation; 'abundant grass' renders the sense of lush, plentiful growth.

pass_b_english: So let us intercede for those who are caught in some transgression, asking that gentleness and humility be given to them, so that they may yield not to us but to the will of God. For in this way their remembrance before God and the saints will be fruitful and complete, accompanied by compassion.
Let us take up discipline, beloved, at which no one should be offended. The admonition we offer one another is good and exceedingly beneficial, for it binds us to the will of God.
For the holy word says: “The Lord disciplined me with discipline, and he did not hand me over to death. For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he whips every son whom he receives.”
“A righteous man will discipline me in mercy,” it says, “and will reprove me, but let not the oil of sinners anoint my head.”

And again it says: “Blessed is the man whom the Lord reproves; do not reject the admonition of the Almighty. For he causes pain, and again he restores; he struck, and his hands healed. Six times he will deliver you from troubles, and in the seventh no evil will touch you. In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war he will release you from the hand of iron. He will hide you from the whip of the tongue, and you will not fear evils when they come. You will laugh at the unrighteous and the lawless, and you will not fear wild beasts; for wild beasts will be at peace with you. Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and the conduct of your tent will not fail. You will know that your offspring is many, and your children like the abundant grass of the field. You will come to the grave like ripe wheat harvested in season, or like a heap on the threshing floor gathered in at the right time.”
You see, beloved, how great is the protection for those who are disciplined by the Master. For being a good Father, he disciplines us so that we may receive mercy through his holy discipline.

problems.why: Greek includes an additional proverb about the Lord loving those He disciplines, which the English skips.
problems.fix: Add after the Proverbs 3:12 quote: “For the Lord loves those He disciplines, and He whips every son He receives.”

problems.quote: the dwelling of your tent will not sin
problems.source_quote: ἡ δὲ δίαιτα τῆς σκηνῆς σου οὐ μὴ ἁμάρτῃ
problems.why: δίαίτα means ‘diet/food’, not ‘dwelling’; the English renders it incorrectly.
problems.fix: Replace with “the food of your tent will not be sinful” (or “the provisions of your tent will not sin”).

problems.source_quote: Παιδεύων ἐπαίδευσέν με ὁ κύριος, καὶ τῷ θανάτῳ οὐ παρέδωκέν με: ὃν γὰρ ἀγαπᾷ κύριος παιδεύει, μαστιγοῖ δὲ πάντα υἱὸν ὃν παραδέχεται.
problems.why: First quote combines Psalm 118:18 (LXX 117:18) and Proverbs 3:12. The citation '(Proverbs 3:12)' only covers the second part, missing Psalm 118:18 attribution for the first sentence.
problems.ruling: Greek mixes two verses (first clause not in Proverbs 3:12); citation only lists Proverbs 3:12, omitting the Psalm source.

problems.ruling: δίατα = way of life, not food; translation misrepresents meaning.
